run.rulesInOwnWords:
Setup: six stages (1 = source, 6 = load). Ratings 10,8,12,6,9,7; upper thresholds 7,6,9,5,7,5; lower thresholds 3,2,4,2,3,2; starting charge 3,6,6,2,2,1; every stage starts CLEAR; the ground tally starts at 0; the breaker setting is 38. Each cycle runs five moves in order, and each move finishes across the whole chain before the next one starts.
1) Charge in: add that cycle's feed to each stage. Ratings are not checked at this point.
2) Shunts: go through stages 1 to 6 in order. If a stage is over its rating, set it to exactly its rating and add the excess to the next stage (i+1). Stage 6's excess goes to ground. Because you walk in order, excess passed down is included when the next stage is checked.
3) Comparators: using the post-shunt charge, a CLEAR stage turns ASSERTED if charge >= its upper threshold. An ASSERTED stage turns CLEAR if charge <= its lower threshold. Otherwise the state stays as it is. Log every flip.
4) Bleed: take a snapshot of all six charges first, then apply every transfer at once. A CLEAR stage loses floor(charge/4) to ground. An ASSERTED stage sends floor(charge/2) to stage i-1, and stage 1's amount goes to ground. States are the ones just set in move 3. Ratings are not checked, so a stage can end above its rating.
5) Breaker: add up the six charges. If the total is strictly greater than 38, every stage becomes floor(charge/2), the total removed goes to ground, and the cycle is recorded as a reset. At 38 or below, nothing happens.

gapsFlagged.rule: Move 4 bleed: which state decides CLEAR leak vs ASSERTED return
gapsFlagged.whatYouAssumed: The state set by this cycle's comparators (move 3) decides it. The write-up's own example of stage 2 ending at 10 on a cycle-5 diode return fits this.
The chain total before halving minus the total after halving (all the floor-halving losses added together) goes to ground.

gapsFlagged.rule: Comparators when a stage is at both thresholds at once / at exactly a threshold
gapsFlagged.whatYouAssumed: Both comparisons include equality ('at or above', 'at or below'). Only one test applies per stage, chosen by its current state, so each stage flips at most once per cycle.
Excess passed down is added before the next stage is checked, so a cascade can run through several stages in a single walk.

run.working:
Format: [s1..s6] ground=G
C1: in [3,12,9,7,5,4] | shunt [3,8,12,6,7,4] G0 (2 dumps 4 into 3; 3 dumps 1 into 4; 4 dumps 2 into 5) | comp: 2,3,4,5 go ASSERTED -> [C,A,A,A,A,C] | bleed [7,10,9,6,4,3] G1 (1 leaks 0; 2 sends 4 to 1; 3 sends 6 to 2; 4 sends 3 to 3; 5 sends 3 to 4; 6 leaks 1) | breaker: sum 39 > 38, halve -> [3,5,4,3,2,1], 21 to ground, G22.
C2: in [7,7,4,4,3,8] | shunt [7,7,4,4,3,7] G23 | comp: 1 goes ASSERTED, 3 goes CLEAR, 5 goes CLEAR, 6 goes ASSERTED -> [A,A,C,A,C,A] | bleed [7,4,5,2,6,4] G27 | breaker: sum 28, no trip.
C3: in [11,8,8,2,6,10] | shunt [10,8,9,2,6,7] G30 | comp: 3 goes ASSERTED, 4 goes CLEAR -> [A,A,A,C,C,A] | bleed [9,8,5,2,8,4] G36 | breaker: sum 36, no trip.
C4: in [16,14,12,3,11,4] | shunt [10,8,12,6,9,7] G44 | comp: 4 goes ASSERTED, 5 goes ASSERTED -> all A | bleed [9,10,9,7,8,4] G49 | breaker: sum 47 > 38, halve -> [4,5,4,3,4,2], 25 to ground, G74.
C5: in [4,11,10,6,7,2] | shunt [4,8,12,6,8,2] G74 | comp: 6 goes CLEAR -> [A,A,A,A,A,C] | bleed [6,10,9,7,4,2] G76 | breaker: sum 38, not strictly over, no trip.
run.balanceCheck: Starting charge 20 + total fed 94 (17+15+17+24+18) = 114. End chain 38 (6+10+9+7+4+2) + ground 76 = 114. It balances.
run.notes: I recomputed everything independently with a short Python script, and it agrees with the write-up's Report paragraph on every figure: end charges, states, flips, breaker cycles 1 and 4, and ground 76. Stage 2 ends at 10, above its rating of 8, because of the cycle-5 diode return. It is reported as read.
